entries.text: Project scaffolded (Vite+React+TS). MediaPipe models + WASM vendored locally. ccmixter.org is egress-blocked from the build sandbox: stems will be fetched by npm run fetch-stems on the user's machine; a generated CC0 demo multitrack ships in-repo so the game is playable now.
Critic round 1 (score 6.5): latency-calibration confidence unusable at 30 fps camera quantisation; pairing radius = outlier cutoff so consistently-late patients yield zero samples.
Critic round 1 (score 7): latencyProbe duplicated engine latency math with different defaults; must delegate to engine estimateLatency.
Critic round 1 (score 6): OneEuro smoothing on raw units gives 13–95 ms lane-dependent lag; filter normalized 0..1 value and route calibration through same pipeline.
Critic round 1 (score 6.5): miss visual can never be seen — gem leaves screen 134 ms after note time but engine declares miss at 210–280 ms.
Subagent spend limit hit mid-loop; resumed workflow after reset (fix rounds + critic rounds 2+ + integration).
Round 2 (6.5): chart lattice gives unbalanced lanes (62/38 at 2 lanes) — bilateral rehab would shortchange one side.
Round 2 (7.5): StemMixer must implement the SongTimeSource contract and return resume start time; pause/resume drifts judgments.
Round 2 (7): VisionInput start/stop not race-safe — StrictMode double-mount leaks two cameras.
Round 2: miss gem culled before the engine ever declares the miss.
PASSED round 5, score 9/10. Judge/scoring/chart generation hold up against a Clone-Hero determinism bar; latency model, lane balance, unmatched-input telemetry and offset rebasing all fixed.
PASSED round 4, score 8.5/10. StemMixer is now the single clock (SongTimeSource), pause/resume sample-accurate, latency probe delegates to the engine, two synthesized CC0 multitracks ship in-repo.
Round 5, score 8.5. Filter moved to normalized units, race-safe camera lifecycle, level-vs-edge trigger bug fixed. Open: pinned-lane watchdog false positives.
Round 4, score 8. Miss visuals now readable at real engine timing, score odometer fixed. Open: receptor ring must read full exactly when the lane would trigger.

Integration complete: full app runs (Home → Mode → Setup → Camera → ROM calibration → Latency → Play → Results → History). 792 tests green. Fetched two real Guitar-Hero-lineage screenshots as reference; blind A/B critic loop now running.
Blind loop round 1: three independent judges rank five unlabelled rhythm-game frames (three ours, two shipped games) without being told which is which.

Blind round 1: ours ranked 2.56 vs shipped games 1.17 (lower is better); 1 of 3 judges put one of ours first. Unanimous deficit: the play field was a postage stamp — vanishing point at 35% of frame height, strike line at 78%, only 2-4 gems on screen, ~55% dead space. Round 2 fix: road now runs near-full height with lane tints and a wider strike line.

Blind round 3: all three judges ranked our three frames ABOVE both shipped reference games, and every judge put one of ours first. Road now fills the frame, 8 gems of read-ahead, beat/bar ladder, gems land on the receptors, crowd and stage lighting. Round 1 ours 2.56 vs refs 1.17; round 3 ours ~1.0 vs refs ~3.5.

Calibration hand-over passed a fresh critic at 8.5/10: a range measured under one camera convention or fingertip can no longer be silently reused for a different lane; the refusal now reaches the therapist on the calibration screen with an actionable reason.

Therapist screens passed clinical-usability critic at 9/10: song preview, per-finger choice for opposition, latency hand-over to the next session, ROM trends across visits, and a real camera-failure screen.
Stem ducking verified end to end in a real browser (npm run critic:audio): player stem 1.0 while hitting, 0.05 after misses, back to 1.0 on the next hit, other stems unmoved.

Receptor biofeedback at 8/10 after 5 rounds — still looping. Open: the picture-in-picture lane meters do not latch the goal state the way the receptor does, so the two meters disagree at the moment of crossing.

Receptor ran 8 fix-and-critique rounds, ending at 8/10. Each round a fresh critic drove the real vision pipeline and found a different real defect: goal cue unreachable on the scripted input path; goal latch outliving the re-arm; the picture-in-picture panel covering the label naming the limb; tracking loss hidden by a mostly-dead stream.

Final review by four independent lenses (patient, therapist, clinical-safety, engineer). All four said they would not ship, and all four independently named the same top blocker: no patient identity anywhere, so a shared clinic tablet pools two people's history, trends and saved ranges. Also: camera never released after a session, two tabs overwriting each other, an interrupted session recording nothing, one weak limb's misses muting the patient's whole instrument, a red failure alarm in a game that cannot be failed, and a results screen that reads as a grade.

Patient identity passed a fresh clinical critic at 8/10. Every session, saved range and progress trend is now scoped to a named patient; existing device records migrate into an 'unassigned' bucket a therapist can rename or reassign; records export off the device; and the stored record carries full clinical movement names instead of the canvas abbreviations.

Ducking is now proportionate and per lane: a weak limb's misses dip the instrument instead of silencing what the strong limb is earning. Round 1 critic found the ROM nudge API built but not wired to the buttons a therapist presses — now fixed and back in review.

Second four-lens review: all four verified every one of the nine earlier blockers actually fixed, by measurement rather than by claim — camera released, per-lane ducking, no failure alarm, honest abandoned-session records, patient identity throughout. Each then found a narrower next tier: no pay-off at the end of a song, a headline range that celebrates the unaffected side, tables that clip silently at tablet width, a dose figure computed per lane but labelled per limb. Now in round three.

Third four-lens review: 2 of 4 would now ship, up from 0 of 4. The patient reviewer: 'the best this app has been, and for the first time it feels like something I would actually want to play tomorrow.' The song now ends with a payoff that leads with movements performed; comparisons against an abandoned session are labelled; tracking quality qualifies the figures it should; time to the first note is 4.1 s, down from 38.7 s. The two holdouts block on narrow, specific things — a 'saved' badge that prints whether or not the write succeeded, a calibration carrying no record of how well it was measured.

Pushed to main. 1654 tests, typecheck, production build, and both browser harnesses green. Four rounds of four-lens review behind it; the last vote was 2 of 4 to ship, with the two holdouts blocking on a 'saved to history' badge that printed whether or not the write succeeded and a calibration that carried no record of how well it was measured — both since addressed, not yet re-voted.
